title: Carbon and Its Compounds: The Chemistry of Life

questions.question: The self-linking of carbon atoms into chains and rings is called:
questions.rationale: Catenation — carbon bonding to carbon — builds molecular backbones; tetravalency sets the four bonds per carbon.

questions.question: Which carbon allotrope conducts electricity?
questions.rationale: Each sp² carbon in graphite contributes a delocalized electron; in diamond the electrons are locked in σ bonds, so it insulates.

questions.question: The hardest naturally occurring substance is:
questions.rationale: Diamond's 3D sp³ network — every carbon bonded to four others — makes it the hardest natural substance.

questions.question: The general formula of the alkynes is:
questions.rationale: One triple bond strips four hydrogens from the alkane formula, giving CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ — e.g., ethyne C₂H₂.

questions.question: Butane (C₄H₁₀) has how many structural isomers?
questions.rationale: n-Butane (straight chain) and iso-butane (branched). Pentane, C₅H₁₂, has three.

questions.question: The functional group of ethanoic acid is:
questions.rationale: The carboxylic acid group –COOH, named with the suffix -oic acid; vinegar is about 5% of it.

questions.question: Pure ethanoic acid is called 'glacial' because it:
questions.rationale: The anhydrous acid solidifies just below room temperature, at about 16.6 °C, into crystals resembling ice.

questions.question: Ethanoic acid + ethanol with an acid catalyst produces:
options: an ester with a sweet smell
questions.rationale: Esterification gives ethyl ethanoate and water; esters carry the fruity, sweet smells of perfumes.

questions.question: Soaps fail in hard water because:
options: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions form an insoluble scum with the soap
questions.rationale: Hardness ions swap for sodium or potassium and precipitate calcium or magnesium salts of the fatty acids — the scum ring.

questions.question: In a soap micelle cleaning grease:
options: heads bury in grease while tails face water
oily tails surround the grease while charged heads face the water
the micelle repels both oil and water
questions.rationale: The micelle locks grease inside its hydrophobic tails while the hydrophilic carboxylate heads keep the whole cluster suspended in water.
